slides.text: After getting laid off from my B2B SaaS product management job, I booked a cheap cabin in the Oregon woods to cry. On my first morning, I wandered into a clearing wearing my gray Patagonia vest, staring at my dead laptop, and muttered aloud, 'We must sunset the legacy ego and pivot toward a scalable, cross-functional paradigm.' Twelve barefoot people picking mushrooms behind a fern immediately fell to their knees.

Apparently, I had stumbled onto a leaderless New Age commune, and fifteen years of corporate Agile training sounds indistinguishable from ancient Tibetan mysticism if you say it with enough dead-eyed exhaustion. When they asked how to achieve inner peace, I drew a kanban board in the dirt with a stick. 'First, we circle back to our core KPIs,' I told them solemnly. 'Then we trim the spiritual backlog in a two-week sprint.'

It’s been four months. My followers—now called The Stakeholders—wake up at dawn for a fifteen-minute Daily Standup Prayer, chant 'Let’s take this offline' before meals, and banish negative energy by placing it in the Parking Lot. Productivity at the organic turnip farm is up three hundred percent, though I did have to excommunicate Brother Caleb for failing to update his astral Jira ticket.
